details:
Tomar NASA Space Apps Challenge project—Haven—er shob gulo core detail ek sathe ekhane sajye dilam, jeta tomader documentation, presentation, ba pitch deck-er jonno khub useful hobe:

Project Overview

  • Project Name: Haven
  • Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge (Dhaka Division, November 2026)
  • Core Concept: An immersive space exploration and data visualization desktop application that combines precise orbital mechanics with deep storytelling centered around historic space missions (Voyager probes and Mars rovers).

Core Themes & Focus Areas

  1. Interactive Planetary Motion: Real-time simulation of celestial bodies, orbital trajectories, and spatial relationships within the solar system.
  2. Deep Space & Surface Missions (Voyager & Mars Rovers): Tracing the historic paths, telemetry, and milestones of humanity's furthest deep-space probes and Martian surface explorers.
  3. Narrative-Driven Exploration: Bridging the gap between raw scientific data and human storytelling to make astrophysics engaging and accessible to everyone.

Technical Stack & Architecture

  • Core Language & Graphics Engine: Built in C++ utilizing SDL2 for high-performance, real-time 2D/3D rendering and smooth frame rates.
  • Platform: Developed on macOS, packaged into a polished, standalone macOS software bundle.
  • UI & Experience: Custom user interface design featuring interactive Earth rotation controls, responsive navigation, and custom vector-based iconography.

Key Features

  • 3D Solar System Simulation: Dynamic visualization of planetary orbits and celestial mechanics.
  • Mission Timelines: Interactive tracking and historical data integration for the Voyager missions and Mars rover expeditions.
  • Custom Desktop Experience: Fully bundled standalone application with custom icons and fluid user controls.
dataRefs: Short Summary: An immersive space exploration and data visualization desktop application that brings interplanetary journeys to life through interactive planetary motion, historical space missions (Voyager & Mars rovers), and engaging narrative storytelling.  Detailed Description: Space exploration yields vast amounts of telemetry, scientific data, and historical milestones, yet translating these complex cosmic achievements into an accessible, engaging format for the general public remains challenging. Our project bridges this vital gap by seamlessly merging scientific accuracy with immersive storytelling and interactive data visualization.  Centered on humanity's most extraordinary exploratory milestones—specifically the legendary Voyager deep-space probes and historic Mars rovers—our application transforms raw celestial telemetry into a dynamic, narrative-driven journey. Users can explore complex planetary orbits, track historical trajectories across the solar system, and witness the monumental scale of space exploration firsthand through an intuitive, interactive interface designed for discovery.  Key Features: Interactive Planetary Motion: A high-performance simulation engine rendering precise orbital mechanics, celestial positioning, and spatial dynamics in real-time.  Mission Chronicles (Voyager & Mars Rovers): Detailed interactive timelines and positional tracking that bring legendary deep-space missions and Martian surface exploration to life.  Immersive Storytelling: Blending hard scientific data with captivating human narratives to educate, engage, and inspire space enthusiasts of all ages.  NASA Data Sources Used: NASA JPL HORIZONS System / Ephemeris Data: Used for high-precision calculations of planetary positions, velocity, and heliocentric trajectories of celestial bodies and deep-space missions (such as Voyager 1 & 2).  NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) & Mission Archives: Integrated historical telemetry, mission logs, and milestones from Mars Exploration Rover (MER) data bundles.  Technical Stack & Architecture: Core Language & Rendering: Built using C++ and SDL2 rendering pipelines for high-performance, ultra-smooth real-time graphics and execution.  Platform: Developed on macOS and packaged into a polished, standalone desktop software bundle.  UI & Experience: Custom user interface design featuring interactive Earth rotation controls, responsive navigation, and custom vector-based iconography.
projectRefs: NASA Space Apps Challenge-e tomar project Haven-er copyright ebong licensing niye kichu important kotha niche diye dilam, jeta tomader GitHub repo ba submission-er jonno khub dorkari hobe:  1. Tomader Code & Intellectual Property (IP): Tomra jehetu Haven project-tar puro code, C++ architecture, ebong UI design nijera baniyecho, ei puro code-er copyright tomader (team-er) kachhe-i thakbe.  NASA Space Apps Challenge-er rules onujayi, competition-e submit korar mane ei na je tomra tomader ownership hariye felcho—tomra nijeder project-er owner thakbe.  2. NASA Data & Public Domain: NASA-r beshirbhag data, ephemeris calculations (JPL HORIZONS), ebong mission archives public domain-e thake.  Tar mane eta use korar jonno kono copyright violation hobe na. Tobe project-er README ba documentation-e "Powered by NASA JPL HORIZONS data" ba proper credit dewa ekta best practice.  3. GitHub-e kon License use korbe? (Recommended) Tomar GitHub repository-te ekta open-source license add kora uchit, jate onnora (ba judges-ra) dekhte pay je code-ta kivabe use kora jabe. Sobcheye bhalo hoy MIT License use korle:  MIT License: Eta ekta khubi permissive license. Mane keu tomar code use ba modify korte parbe, kintu tomader credit dite hobe ebong tomra kono liability (risk) বহন korbe na.  GitHub repo create korar somoy "Add a README file" er pashe "Add .gitignore" ebong "Choose a license" (select MIT) option-e click korlei automatic LICENSE file toiri hoye jabe.  Summary: Tomra project-er owner thakbe, NASA data freely use kora jay credit diye, ebong GitHub-e ekta MIT License add kore dilei shob safe and clean thakbe! Kono license file ba README setup korte help lagle bolte paro.
